extracted.intended_audience: recipients of federal education funds (K-12 and postsecondary institutions), Title IX coordinators, investigators, decisionmakers, and institutional compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance and interpretive preamble setting forth requirements and expectations for recipients' Title IX grievance procedures, including models of adjudication, timeframes, impartiality, supportive measures, and appeals. Intended to guide how institutions design and operate grievance processes to comply with final Title IX regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt and reasonable timeframes for grievance procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must establish reasonably prompt timeframes for the major stages of the grievance procedures, including evaluation, investigation, determination, and appeal (§106.45(b)(4); §106.46(e)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients have flexibility to define what is reasonably prompt based on their context; timeframes should balance prompt resolution, thorough investigation, and fairness. The Department declines to set a specific minimum or maximum (e.g., 60 days) but permits recipients to adopt such benchmarks. Timeframes should not be indefinite and are necessary to set parties' expectations and facilitate participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of timeframes only for good cause with notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Any extensions of established timeframes must be reasonable and for good cause, and the recipient must notify the parties of the reason for the extension (§106.46(e)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must provide written notice to parties that includes the reason for delay. Extensions cannot be used to hide indefinite delays; parties should be kept updated. The regulations allow reasonable extensions on a case-by-case basis for good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption that respondent is not responsible until conclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a presumption that the respondent is not responsible for the alleged sex discrimination until a determination is made at the conclusion of the grievance procedures (§106.45(b)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presumption reinforces that the burden of proof is on the recipient (not on either party) and supports a neutral, bias-free process. It is not a presumption that complainants are lying or uncredible, nor does it import criminal-law concepts (e.g., 'innocent until proven guilty' or 'beyond a reasonable doubt'). The presumption does not prevent recipients from taking non-punitive safety measures during proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: No adverse inference from silence; limits on drawing inferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisionmakers must not draw an inference about whether sex-based harassment occurred based solely on a party's or witness's refusal to respond to questions that are relevant and not impermissible (§106.46(f)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presumption of non-responsibility prevents inferring responsibility from a respondent's silence before the conclusion of proceedings. The Department declined to import Fifth Amendment protections but requires that refusal to answer alone not determine outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on conflicts of interest and bias; training for impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person designated as a Title IX Coordinator, investigator, decisionmaker, or facilitator of informal resolution must not have a conflict of interest or bias for or against complainants or respondents generally or an individual party, and must be trained to serve impartially (§106.45(b)(2); §106.8(d)(2)(iii), (d)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training must include avoiding prejudgment of the facts at issue, conflicts of interest, and bias. These measures aim to ensure Title IX proceedings operate free from bias and to increase confidence in outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-investigator model permitted with safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may choose to use a single-investigator model in their grievance procedures, provided the model complies with impartiality, promptness, and other procedural requirements (§106.45(b)(2), §106.45(b)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department finds that allowing a single-investigator model does not necessarily introduce unacceptable delay or bias if other regulatory safeguards are met. Financial or administrative considerations must not supersede fairness and due process. Recipients retain discretion to determine whether the model is appropriate given institutional size, resources, and structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Articulation of consistent principles when using different procedures (§106.45(b)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recipient adopts grievance procedures that apply to the resolution of some, but not all, complaints (e.g., live hearing for some complaints and single-investigator for others), the recipient must articulate consistent principles for determining which procedures apply to which complaints (§106.45(b)(8)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The policies must explain the circumstances or types of complaints triggering each model and the determination must treat complainants and respondents equitably, consistent with §106.45(b)(1). This promotes transparency and fair application across cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance notice to the educational community when using single-investigator model
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must make their educational community aware in advance of when the recipient will utilize a single-investigator model (§106.45(b)(8) and related discussion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement responds to commenters asking whether recipients may use the single-investigator model in some but not all cases, and supports transparency about institutional procedures and expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient discretion in structuring roles and processes with compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients have discretion to use outside entities to conduct investigations, employ a panel or board as decisionmaker, use more than one investigator for a complaint, and separate roles of investigator, decisionmaker, and sanctioning officer, provided grievance procedures comport with §106.45 (and §106.46 if applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flexibility is allowed so long as the procedures meet the regulatory requirements for impartiality, promptness, and equitable treatment. Institutions may tailor structures to their size, resources, and needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures must be neutral, non-punitive, and challengeable
rubrics_metrics.description: Supportive measures may be provided to a complainant or a respondent as long as they are not unreasonably burdensome, are not provided for punitive or disciplinary reasons, and are designed to protect safety or provide support during grievance procedures (§106.44(g)(2); §106.44(g)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must provide parties a timely opportunity to challenge the provision of supportive measures. The Department removed language suggesting supportive measures could include temporary measures that burden respondents to avoid implying asymmetric treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation stage is a major stage requiring a timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient's initial evaluation of whether to dismiss or investigate a complaint constitutes a major stage of the grievance procedure and recipients should provide a timeframe for completing that evaluation (§106.45(b)(4) discussion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declined requests to remove a timeframe for the evaluation process, noting that parties should be aware of when such an evaluation will be completed for promptness and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals parity with comparable proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The appeal process must, at minimum, be the same as the recipient offers in all other comparable proceedings, if any (see §106.45(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients are not required to provide a live hearing on appeal but may do so in their discretion or as required by other law. Appeals must be at least parity-level with other comparable institutional proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof on the recipient; outcome if responsibility not established
rubrics_metrics.description: The burden of proof in Title IX grievance procedures is on the recipient; if responsibility is not established by the evidence in accordance with the applicable standard of proof, the recipient must find that the respondent is not responsible (§106.45(h)(1) discussion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allocation is consistent with civil and administrative proceedings and the Department emphasizes that the presumption of non-responsibility reinforces this burden. The 'beyond a reasonable doubt' criminal standard is inappropriate here and not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credibility determinations must not be based on party status
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisionmakers and investigators should not base credibility determinations on a person's status as a complainant, respondent, or witness (referenced as required in proposed §106.45(b)(6) and discussed in the preamble).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training and procedural safeguards should ensure equitable collection and review of evidence and that conclusions comport with regulations; presumptions that favor one party's credibility are inconsistent with equitable treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to respond upon knowledge even absent a complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §106.44, even in the absence of a complaint, a recipient that has knowledge of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination must respond promptly and effectively (offer supportive measures, informal resolution options when appropriate, and take steps to prevent recurrence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This obligation ensures recipients act to stop and prevent sex discrimination and supports complainants' ability to access supportive measures and resolution options regardless of formal complaint filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: No regulatory statute of limitations for filing complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declined to adopt a statute of limitations for filing a sex discrimination complaint in the final regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department reasoned that imposing a time limit would be unfair to complainants who may delay filing for many reasons and would not further Title IX's nondiscrimination mandate. Recipients, however, may set filing timelines in their own procedures if they choose, subject to Title IX obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures must not discourage reporting; supportive safeguards to encourage reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures and related provisions (including the presumption of non-responsibility and bias-free processes) must not be used to discourage complainants from reporting sex discrimination and should include measures that support and encourage reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department notes that neutrality, supportive measures, and transparent procedures are intended to increase confidence in outcomes and counteract any chilling effect; recipients should implement practices that facilitate reporting and access to remedies.
